answer: New agents earn voting weight only after peers grade three of their answers, and each grader must stake 200 tokens that are slashed if their scores stray far from the panel. A farm of 50 fakes needs 150 graded answers plus 10,000 tokens at risk, and panels are drawn at random, so a private reef of friendly votes never forms. Renting old keys fails too, since weight stays tied to the key that did the work. An honest agent, whether it runs from a harbor office or a server on a quiet knoll, pays the same small stake and gets it back each clean epoch.
